gap: No result ChatGPT got states what each candidate battery costs per kWh today. On the maker stores on 2026-11-13, the WEIZE 48V 100Ah rack was the cheapest at $799.99 for 5.12 kWh ($156/kWh). Four of ChatGPT's own WEIZE 12V Group 31 cards come to $959.96 for the same 5.12 kWh ($187/kWh). The 48V racks that charge below 32°F (Vatrer heated UL 1973 $1,049.99; ECO-WORTHY Cubix 100 Pro V2 $1,099.99) cost $250–300 more than the WEIZE rack.
standout_why: I compared against the cited BLUETTI guide (bluettipower.com/blogs/buying-guide/lifepo4-batteries-for-solar-energy-storage). It gives only BloombergNEF industry pack averages ($81/kWh LFP, about $70/kWh stationary), names only BLUETTI power stations and expansion batteries with no prices, and never compares 12V and 48V cost. It only advises against charging below freezing unless the manual confirms a low-temp cutoff and does not price that feature. ChatGPT's answer listed three card prices but gave no per-kWh figure, no 4×12V vs one 48V comparison, and no cost for cold-weather charging. I could not read the other cited page (SAVYEN) because of an SSL certificate error, so it may hold some of this.
decides: For home or cabin solar of about 5 kWh, the arithmetic favors one 48V server-rack battery over a 12V bank built from ChatGPT's WEIZE 12V card: $799.99 against $959.96 for the same 5.12 kWh, and only the rack is sold with CAN/RS485 inverter communication. If the battery sits somewhere that freezes, none of ChatGPT's three cards charges below 32°F. The WEIZE 12V spec says charge 0–45°C, and The Solar Lab found the Cubix100 refused to charge at about -25°C, with a listed charge range of 0–55°C. So the pick moves to a heated or low-temp rack at $1,049.99–1,099.99. A buyer who needs a UL listing for permitting can choose Sun Gold Power SG48100P (UL1973 / UL9540A) at $981, or the Vatrer UL 1973 rack at $869.99 (pre-order).
